$comment: See claude.json for the schema rationale. Note how much thinner this is — Codex needs no companion_writes and no sidecar identity, because its tokens are self-describing JWTs.
surfaces_note: desktop sharing is strong inference, not documented: ChatGPT.app bundles the identical binary and stores its non-credential state in ~/.codex

_all_platforms.mode_caveat: applied only at creation; an existing file with looser permissions is rewritten without being re-chmod'd
_all_platforms.note: same path on darwin, linux and win32 — no XDG, no %APPDATA%

_optional_keyring.default_note: plaintext file is the out-of-box behaviour; keyring is opt-in

_win32_keyring_variant.reason: credential-manager per-entry size limit (inferred, not stated in source)

config_dir_env.name: CODEX_HOME
config_dir_env.strict_note: if set, the directory must already exist or Codex errors out

credential.api_key_note: the only always-serialized field; null under OAuth. API-key and OAuth share one file, discriminated by auth_mode.
credential.parser_trap: id_token is a struct in the Rust source but a BARE JWT STRING on disk

fallback.used_when: the JWT exp claim cannot be parsed

observed_lifetimes.refresh_token: no local expiry recorded; server decides

identity.note: self-contained — no sidecar file, no server call, no splice step

companion_writes_note: none. auth.json is the whole story.

policy.danger: a snapshot taken before a refresh is DEAD — the old refresh token was invalidated by the rotation. Restoring it silently breaks the account until the user re-logs in.

adjacent_store.name: MCP server OAuth
adjacent_store.fallback_file_warning: same FILENAME as Claude's user credentials, entirely different purpose
